source.title_on_document: Scientific exploration, collaboration and labor division in the large language model era

supplement.where: Supplementary Materials on PDF pp. 22-46 (numbered S1-S25)
supplement.holds: Supplementary Notes 1-2 (AI-writing fraction estimator; fixed-effect event-study models with author-clustered SEs), Figures S1-S13 (alternative measures, topic Gini, event-study coefficients S5 and S9, figure only), Tables S1-S4 (paper and author counts, field distribution of high/low AI-writing groups, CEM balance)

paper_design_summary: Descriptive bibliometric study. The authors link PubMed Central full text to OpenAlex histories for 775,323 seed authors and compare field breadth, exploration of new fields, and collaborator diversity in 2023-2025 with pre-2023 linear trends, and between CEM-matched authors with high and low AI-writing fractions (a word-frequency proxy for LLM-assisted writing). A second dataset of 137,120 multi-author PLOS and PMC papers with CRediT statements tracks the division of contribution roles before and after 2022. Nobody is assigned to AI; the authors state the design is descriptive and not causal.

studies.label: PMC-OpenAlex author panel (research portfolios, exploration, collaboration), 2011-2025

participants.exclusions: Seed authors identified from 2023-2025 PMC papers (3,959,771 candidates); kept only authors with at least three matched PMC seed works and at least three OpenAlex publications before 2022; excluded papers with more than 20 authors and the top 2% of candidate seed authors by all-time publication count (PDF p. 15, Data). For the high/low AI-writing comparison, Results p. 6 reports 244,062 high and 211,911 low authors before annual CEM matching and uses rates above 0.15 and below 0.05. Methods p. 16, Fig. S9 p. 36, and Table S4 p. 45 instead specify inclusive thresholds of at least 0.15 and at most 0.05; see open_questions. The middle band is excluded from that comparison. Retained matched-sample counts are not reported.
participants.who: Publishing scientists (seed authors of PubMed Central papers, mostly biomedical) and their full OpenAlex publication histories: 26,057,772 works and 18,499,462 distinct coauthors
participants.country: Multi-country (largest shares: China 27.2%, United States 14.8%; Table S2)
participants.quote: The final dataset contains 775,323 seed authors.

ai_tool.name_model: Not identified; LLM use proxied by each paper's estimated AI-writing fraction (word-frequency mixture MLE following Liang et al., with bioRxiv word probabilities)
ai_tool.how_used: No observed tool use. Exposure is the calendar period (after 2022) or an author's mean AI-writing fraction across 2023-2025 papers (Supplementary Note 1, p. 23).

task.description: Scientists' publishing record: fields of their papers, fields of cited references, entry into new fields, and collaborators' fields

outcomes.name: Interdisciplinarity of an author's publication portfolio (Rao-Stirling index on papers' primary fields)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Rao-Stirling combines an author's shares of papers across fields with cosine distances between fields derived from co-citation patterns (PDF pp. 15-16). Distinct-field count and Shannon entropy are grouped here as alternative summaries of within-author portfolio breadth. Further breadth variants are focal-field HHI, top-field share, reference-field Rao-Stirling, and the share of cited references outside the citing paper's field (Fig. S1a-d, pp. 26-27/S5-S6); these characterize field breadth, not rated creativity. The Results report the last measure as 37.4% in 2025, 6.1% above the extrapolated trend (p. 3). Fig. 1 caption p. 4 specifies 95% bootstrap confidence intervals; no numerical interval bounds are printed.

contrasts.control_arm: Publication year 2022 and the 2011-2022 linear trend extrapolated
contrasts.reported: Rao-Stirling index rose "from 0.176 in 2022 to 0.199 in 2025; by 2025, it was 13.0% higher than the value expected under the pre-2023 trend". Related breadth measures: distinct primary fields 2.3 (2022) to 2.8 (2025), 15.6% above trend; Shannon entropy 0.55 to 0.71.
contrasts.locator: p. 3, Results; Fig. 1a-c p. 4; event-study with author FE in Fig. S5 p. 31 (S10)

contrasts.treatment_arm: Higher author AI-writing rate (continuous association; no assigned treatment or CEM matching)
contrasts.control_arm: Lower author AI-writing rate (association comparator; no assigned control)
contrasts.reported: Author-level association: Rao-Stirling index and AI-writing rate r = 0.237, p < 0.001. The Results report mean AI-writing rates of 0.143 for the first Rao-Stirling decile and 0.230 for the tenth. These values are retained as reported in the text; Fig. 2b instead labels the deciles by author AI-writing rate, so the conditioning variable is unresolved (see open_questions). These are not estimates of the CEM-matched high-versus-low comparison.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 6, AI-writing intensity and portfolio breadth, second paragraph; p. 7, Fig. 2b and caption

outcomes.name: Exploration: share of authors publishing in at least one field where they had not published before
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Annual share of authors entering at least one previously unpublished primary field (Fig. 1d, p. 4). The number of new primary fields entered is grouped here as the count variant of the same field-entry outcome; the Results describe the same post-2022 increase and show it in Fig. S1f without exact endpoint values (p. 5; pp. 26-27/S5-S6).

contrasts.control_arm: Publication year 2022 and the 2011-2022 linear trend extrapolated
contrasts.reported: Authors publishing in at least one field where they had not previously published: 35.5% in 2025 versus 30.4% in 2022; the 2025 level was 23.2% above the extrapolated pre-2023 trend.

outcomes.name: Research pivot size (cosine distance between a paper's reference fields and the author's prior three-year reference profile)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Cosine distance between the focal paper's reference-field counts and the author's reference-field counts from the previous three publication years, excluding same-year papers; averaged across eligible papers per author-year (PDF p. 16). This measures movement from an author's prior research profile, not similarity across different people's outputs.

contrasts.control_arm: Publication year 2022 and the 2011-2022 linear trend extrapolated
contrasts.reported: Pivot "declining from 0.236 in 2011 to 0.226 in 2022 before increasing to 0.242 in 2025"
contrasts.locator: p. 5, Results; Fig. 1f p. 4; method p. 16

contrasts.treatment_arm: Higher author AI-writing rate (continuous association; no assigned treatment or CEM matching)
contrasts.control_arm: Lower author AI-writing rate (association comparator; no assigned control)
contrasts.reported: Author-level association: pivot size and AI-writing rate r = 0.230, p < 0.001. The Results report pivot size of 0.172 in the first decile and 0.295 in the tenth, immediately after describing Rao-Stirling deciles. Fig. 2b instead labels author AI-writing-rate deciles. The values are retained as reported in the text without resolving that inconsistency (see open_questions); they are not estimates of the CEM-matched high-versus-low comparison.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 6, AI-writing intensity and portfolio breadth, second paragraph; p. 7, Fig. 2b and caption

outcomes.name: Portfolio interdisciplinarity (Rao-Stirling) by author AI-writing rate, high vs low AI-writing authors (CEM-matched)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Rao-Stirling index on authors' publication fields, compared in annually CEM-matched high/low author-year samples. Matching uses career stage, primary field, affiliation-country group, and trailing productivity bins; only strata containing both groups are retained and weighted (PDF pp. 16-17; Table S4 p. 45/S24). The group totals on p. 6 precede annual matching; the retained matched sample size is not reported, so n_units remains null. The continuous associations are recorded separately under S1-O1 and S1-O3.

contrasts.treatment_arm: High-AI-writing authors, annually CEM-matched: Methods rate at least 0.15; Results reports 244,062 authors before matching (strict/inclusive cutoff inconsistency; see open_questions)
contrasts.control_arm: Low-AI-writing authors, annually CEM-matched: Methods rate at most 0.05; Results reports 211,911 authors before matching (strict/inclusive cutoff inconsistency; see open_questions)
contrasts.reported: Matched high-AI-writing authors were already more interdisciplinary before 2023, and the gap widened afterward (Results p. 6; Fig. 2f). Fig. 2f plots annual group means and high-minus-low differences with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals; exact matched estimates and interval bounds are not printed. Fig. S9 plots CEM-weighted high-minus-low event-study coefficients relative to the 2022 gap, controlling for author and year fixed effects and annual publication counts, with author-clustered standard errors and 95% confidence intervals. Exact coefficient and interval values, and retained matched-sample counts, are not reported numerically.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 6, matched comparisons; p. 7, Fig. 2f and caption; pp. 16-17, High- and Low-AI-Writing Author Matching; p. 24 (S3), Supplementary Note 2; p. 36 (S15), Fig. S9; p. 45 (S24), Table S4

outcomes.name: Topic concentration of papers within broad fields (Gini index over OpenAlex primary topics)
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Gini index of annual publication counts over OpenAlex primary topics, separately for each broad field. Fig. S6a uses the fixed set of 3,731 topics present as primary topics in every sample year (PDF pp. 32-33/S11-S12).

contrasts.control_arm: Pre-2023 publication years, with 2022 as the last pre-period year
contrasts.reported: Results p. 5 states that topic Gini declined in major fields after 2022. Fig. S6a presents five separate field series, with differing trajectories: Environmental Science ends above its 2022 Gini level, while Medicine and Agricultural and Biological Sciences end below theirs. These are qualitative readings of the plotted trajectories, not numerical effect estimates. Exact endpoints, uncertainty, and a pooled across-field change are not printed. Lower Gini means greater diversity, but the combined field entry is coded mixed.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 5, topic-diversity paragraph; p. 32 (S11), Fig. S6a trajectories; p. 33 (S12), Fig. S6a caption

diversity_detail.metric: Gini index of annual paper counts across OpenAlex primary topics within each broad field
diversity_detail.embedding_model: not_applicable; OpenAlex topic categories, with no embedding model used for this metric
diversity_detail.computed_over: Annual publication pools within five broad fields: Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology; Agricultural and Biological Sciences; Medicine; Environmental Science; Engineering. The fixed set contains 3,731 topics observed as primary topics in every sample year; this is a category count, not a count of people or outputs.
diversity_detail.uncertainty: not_stated; Fig. S6a and its caption give no numerical uncertainty or uncertainty-estimation procedure
diversity_detail.notes: Lower Gini means greater topic dispersion. The authors' Results summary describes declining concentration, but the plotted field trajectories do not all show the same direction relative to 2022. No pooled across-field estimate is reported; direction is coded mixed. No values have been digitized.

outcomes.name: Dispersion of out-of-field publishing destinations (coefficient of variation)
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Collective dispersion of cross-field publishing within broad fields. Results p. 5 describes destinations of authors' out-of-field publications; Fig. S6b caption describes dispersion in the shares of authors publishing in different fields within each broad field. The source gives no explicit formula, so this wording difference is retained (PDF pp. 32-33/S11-S12).

contrasts.control_arm: Pre-2023 publication years, with 2022 as the last pre-period year
contrasts.reported: The Results state that the coefficient of variation in out-of-field publishing destinations fell after 2022. Fig. S6b ends below the 2022 level in each of the five broad-field series, although some series initially rise in 2023. Lower coefficient of variation is interpreted as more evenly distributed cross-field publishing, so direction is reversed to diversity higher. No exact endpoint values, numerical uncertainty, or pooled change are printed.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 5, topic and cross-field diversity paragraph; p. 32 (S11), Fig. S6b; p. 33 (S12), Fig. S6b caption

diversity_detail.metric: Coefficient of variation in cross-field publishing shares within each broad field
diversity_detail.embedding_model: not_applicable; field-category shares, with no embedding model used for this metric
diversity_detail.computed_over: Annual cross-field publishing shares for authors within each of five broad fields: Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology; Agricultural and Biological Sciences; Medicine; Environmental Science; Engineering. Results describe dispersion across destinations; the caption describes shares of authors publishing in different fields.
diversity_detail.uncertainty: not_stated; Fig. S6b and its caption give no numerical uncertainty or uncertainty-estimation procedure
diversity_detail.notes: Lower coefficient of variation indicates a more even spread of cross-field publishing; the sign is reversed to diversity higher. The precise formula is not given, and no endpoint estimates are digitized.

outcomes.name: Average distance between a paper's field and the author's primary field
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Field-level cosine distance based on binary reference vectors over citing papers, summarized over authors' papers (PDF pp. 15-16; Fig. 1e p. 4). The author's primary field is assigned from cumulative publication history through the focal year (p. 15). The share of papers outside the author's primary field is grouped here as an incidence variant of the same departure from the primary field (Fig. S1e, pp. 26-27/S5-S6). The outcome-specific author-year count is not printed.

contrasts.control_arm: Publication year 2022 and the extrapolated 2011-2022 linear trend
contrasts.reported: Average field distance reached 0.255 in 2025, 13.0% above the value expected from the pre-2023 trend. The Results do not print its 2022 value. Fig. 1e shows the trajectory with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals but no numerical interval bounds. The related share of papers outside the author's primary field rose from 39.7% in 2022 to 44.6% in 2025 (Results p. 3; Fig. S1e).
contrasts.locator: PDF pp. 3 and 5, Research portfolios and exploration expanded after 2022; p. 4, Fig. 1e and caption; pp. 26-27 (S5-S6), Fig. S1e

outcomes.name: New-agenda lead publications per author (count and share from bibliographic coupling)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Papers in each author's co-reference network are linked by shared references, and Louvain communities define research agendas; the earliest papers in an agenda are new-agenda leads. The count and share are grouped as absolute and normalized versions of the same agenda-entry measure. Isolate-inclusive and isolate-excluding networks are robustness variants, retained in separate contrasts because their plotted directions differ. Restricted to authors with at least 10 publications in the full sample; the number of retained authors is not reported (10 is a publication threshold, not a participant count). Shaded bands denote 95% confidence intervals across authors; the interval-estimation procedure and bounds are not stated (PDF p. 28/S7, Fig. S2).

contrasts.treatment_arm: Post-2022 publication years (2023-2025), counting isolated papers as singleton agendas
contrasts.control_arm: Pre-2023 publication years, with 2022 as the last pre-period year; same isolate-inclusive definition
contrasts.reported: Fig. S2 shows rising mean counts and shares of new-agenda lead publications after 2022 in the isolate-inclusive series. The caption interprets this as renewed entry into bibliographically distinct agendas, partly driven by isolated papers. Exact endpoint means and confidence-interval bounds are not printed.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 5, new research agendas paragraph; p. 28 (S7), Fig. S2 solid blue series and caption

contrasts.treatment_arm: Post-2022 publication years (2023-2025), excluding isolated papers before identifying agenda leads
contrasts.control_arm: Pre-2023 publication years, with 2022 as the last pre-period year; same isolate-excluding definition
contrasts.reported: The dotted gold series in Fig. S2 declines after 2022 for both the mean count and share of new-agenda lead publications when isolated papers are excluded. This is a qualitative reading of the plotted trajectories; no endpoint estimates or interval bounds are digitized.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 28 (S7), Fig. S2 dotted gold series and caption

studies.label: CRediT contribution-role dataset (PLOS and PMC multi-author papers), 2018-2025

participants.who: Corpus of 137,120 multi-author papers (128,613 PLOS, 8,507 other PMC-indexed journals) with CRediT contribution statements, 945,989 paper-author observations
participants.quote: The final dataset contains 137,120 multi-author papers, including 128,613 from PLOS journals and 8,507 from other PMC-indexed journals, covering 945,989 paper-author observations

ai_tool.name_model: Not identified; paper-level AI-writing fraction used as proxy
ai_tool.how_used: Exposure is the period after 2022 or the paper's AI-writing fraction

task.description: Division of reported contribution roles (14 CRediT categories) among coauthors

eligibility.reason: S1 analyzes publication histories for 775,323 seed authors (PDF p. 15, Data), exceeding the people-count threshold, and computes topic concentration and cross-field dispersion from real papers across time (p. 5; Fig. S6a-b, pp. 32-33/S11-S12). These computed collective-diversity outcomes satisfy the codebook's observational context definition and output-scoring criterion; a human creativity rating is not required (creativity-codebook.md, section 3). No people are randomly assigned to AI, and exposure is inferred from calendar period or AI-writing signals; the authors explicitly describe the design as descriptive and noncausal (p. 3; p. 14, Limitations; pp. 16-17, matching). Criterion 1 therefore fails and core remains no. S2's contribution-role overlap is not a creativity or output-diversity outcome (p. 17, Pairwise Role-Set Similarity).

one_line_finding: Among 775,323 mostly biomedical scientists, portfolio interdisciplinarity (Rao-Stirling) rose from 0.176 in 2022 to 0.199 in 2025, 13.0% above the pre-2023 trend, and the share entering a new field rose from 30.4% to 35.5% (p. 3, Fig. 1), with larger and widening gaps for high- versus low-AI-writing authors that already existed before 2023 (p. 6, Fig. 2).
open_questions: AI-writing group boundaries are internally inconsistent. Results p. 6 defines high as exceeding 0.15 and low as below 0.05, whereas Methods p. 16, Fig. S9 caption p. 36 (S15), and Table S4 note p. 45 (S24) use at least 0.15 and at most 0.05. Matched-comparison labels follow the Methods with this caveat; inclusion of authors exactly at the boundaries cannot be confirmed.

Decile definitions are internally inconsistent. Results p. 6 describes first and tenth Rao-Stirling deciles with mean AI-writing rates 0.143 and 0.230, then gives pivot sizes 0.172 and 0.295. Fig. 2b's horizontal axis and caption on p. 7 instead specify author AI-writing-rate deciles. The text's values and labels are retained only as reported, in the association contrasts for S1-O1 and S1-O3; the conditioning variable cannot be resolved from this document.
